passage:
When Harish got the offer from the design studio, the whole group chat lit up. Farhan typed "Congrats!" and put on a smile at the tea stall, but a small, cold feeling sat under his ribs, and he heard his own voice say, "Must be nice." Harish glanced at him, then looked away.

Harish had noticed the coolness in the last few days. The joking had slowed, and there were sarcastic little comments. He felt a pinch of hurt. He did not pretend the offer was nothing, and he did not start talking about it every five minutes either. He kept his voice normal and asked, "How's your portfolio going?" and let Farhan give a one-word answer.

That night Farhan opened his notebook and wrote, "I'm jealous." He read the line, and it looked less frightening on paper. The next line came more easily: "I want to work on products people use, not just get the same job as everybody." He closed the notebook, and the smallness eased a little.

The next morning he found Harish at the gate. "I was a jerk yesterday. I'm really glad for you, honestly. Tell me about the studio." Jomon, who had been listening, raised an eyebrow, then grinned. Harish laughed. "It has a very bad coffee machine."

qa.q: What kind of studio made Harish the offer?
How did Farhan's envy and Harish's response fit together, and what did the notebook change?
qa.a: Farhan smiled but said must be nice, and Harish noticed the coolness, stayed warm and did not hide his news. In the notebook Farhan admitted his envy and worked out what he wanted, so he could congratulate Harish honestly.

qa.q: What was Farhan feeling at the tea stall when he typed Congrats?
qa.a: He felt small and envious while smiling, with a cold feeling under his ribs.

qa.q: What could Harish do if Farhan is still a bit distant next month?
qa.a: He can stay warm without hiding his progress, and give Farhan room and time.

grounding: A friend's job offer is seen from the friend who feels small while smiling and the friend whose success creates distance.
